documents.title: Dermatology Surveillance Visit
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatology follow-up, date of service 01/17/2025. Received 01/21/2025.

Ms. Lambert returns six months after wide local excision of a stage IA melanoma of the back (pT1a, Breslow 0.6 mm). She reports no new or changing spots and no lumps.

Allergies: penicillin (rash); dust mites. Medications: cetirizine, sumatriptan as needed.

Full skin examination: the excision scar on the back is well healed, flat and without pigment, nodularity or satellite lesions. No new atypical or suspicious lesions elsewhere. Cervical, axillary and inguinal nodes not palpable.

Assessment: history of melanoma, no evidence of recurrence.

Plan: continue monthly self-examination and sun protection. Return in 6 months for full skin examination.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning - the pharmacy says I'm out of refills on both the cetirizine and the sumatriptan. Same doses as always. Thank you!

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Beth, the doctor approved both: cetirizine 10 mg daily, 90 days with 3 refills, and sumatriptan 50 mg, 9 tablets with 5 refills. They should be ready later today.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she's at her office, consented, ID verified.

Her usual spring allergies have come on hard the last 10 days with the warm stretch: sneezing, runny nose, itchy watery eyes, worse after her lunchtime walks. Still taking cetirizine daily. No fever, facial pain, wheeze or shortness of breath. Not sick otherwise.

On video: comfortable, mild conjunctival injection, speaking full sentences, no distress.

A/P: seasonal allergic rhinitis, typical flare at peak tree pollen. Keep the cetirizine. Shower and change after time outside, windows closed, saline rinse twice a day, take the cetirizine in the evening so it covers the morning peak. Dust mite covers already in place. She'll message if not settling by mid-May.

documents.title: Dermatology Surveillance Visit
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatology follow-up, date of service 07/18/2025. Received 07/22/2025.

One year from treatment of stage IA melanoma of the back. No concerns today; doing monthly skin checks with a mirror and photos.

Allergies: penicillin, dust mites.

Exam: total body skin examination. Scar intact and unremarkable. No new suspicious pigmented lesions. No palpable lymphadenopathy in the nodal basins.

Assessment and plan: no evidence of recurrence. Next full skin examination in 6 months. Sun protection reinforced for the summer.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, 43F. Good year.

- Melanoma, stage IA back, WLE 7/2024: derm visits Jan and July both clear. Doing her own monthly checks.
- Migraine w/o aura: unchanged, a few a month, sumatriptan works. Uses well under the monthly supply.
- Allergic rhinitis: spring flare in April settled with the non-drug measures; cetirizine daily.

Meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily; sumatriptan 50 mg prn. Allergies: penicillin (rash), dust mites.
Social: never smoker; 1-2 drinks/wk; still in the lab.

Exam: NAD. Vitals ok. HEENT unremarkable. No cervical, supraclavicular or axillary adenopathy. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign, no hepatosplenomegaly. Back scar well healed, no pigment or nodules. Skin survey otherwise benign-appearing. Neuro nonfocal.

PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

Plan:
- CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c today.
- Flu and COVID vaccines today.
- Mammogram in November, ordered.
- Colorectal screening: turns 45 in June 2027 - we'll go over options at next year's physical.
- Pap/HPV next due 2029. Tdap due 2028.
- Continue derm q6mo.

Next physical fall 2026.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Beth - your labs from Tuesday are all within the normal range: blood count, kidney, liver, A1c, cholesterol. No changes. Have a good fall.

reports.text: Bilateral screening digital breast tomosynthesis. Compared with 11/19/2024 and earlier. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion. Stable.
reports.conclusion: Negative screening mammogram. BI-RADS 1. Annual screening.

documents.title: Mammogram Result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Your mammogram on the 18th was normal. Next due November 2026.

documents.title: Records Request - Occupational Health
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Fax received from her employer's occupational health service requesting a medical summary ahead of a protocol clearance visit on 12/19, with a signed authorization from the patient. Called pt to confirm she wants it sent - yes. Routed to PCP to prepare.

documents.title: Medical Summary for Occupational Health
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To the occupational health physician:

At the request of our patient, Ms. Beth Lambert (DOB 06/26/1982), and with her written authorization, I am providing a summary of her care.

Problems: seasonal allergic rhinitis; migraine without aura, episodic; melanoma of the back, superficial spreading, Breslow 0.6 mm, stage IA, treated with wide local excision 07/2024 with clear margins, under dermatology surveillance every 6 months with no recurrence to date.
Surgical history: tonsillectomy in childhood; wisdom teeth extraction.
Medications: cetirizine 10 mg daily; sumatriptan 50 mg as needed for migraine.
Allergies: penicillin (rash); dust mites.
Immunizations: Tdap 2018; influenza and COVID-19 current as of 09/2025.
Most recent labs (09/2025) normal.

She has no condition that I am aware of that would limit her work. Please contact the office with questions.

Primary Care

documents.title: Occupational Health Clearance
documents.author: occupational health
documents.body:
Occupational health consultation, date of service 12/19/2025. Copy to primary care, received 12/23/2025.

Reason for visit: medical clearance for participation in a research protocol, with a systematic health assessment.

Employee: Beth Lambert, biomedical research scientist (PhD).

History reviewed with the employee and with the primary care summary of 12/10/2025:
- Melanoma of the back, treated in 2024, under dermatology follow-up
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis
- Migraine without aura
Surgical: tonsillectomy at 7; wisdom teeth removed at 18.
Medications: cetirizine 10 mg by mouth daily; sumatriptan 50 mg by mouth as needed for migraine.
Allergies: penicillin (cutaneous rash); dust mites.
Family: mother with hypertension; father with type 2 diabetes; maternal grandmother with breast cancer at 68; no family history of melanoma or skin cancer.
Social: never smoker; alcohol occasional, 1-2 drinks per week.

Assessment: health assessment completed. No medical condition identified that would restrict her participation.

Determination: medically cleared for the protocol without restrictions. She was asked to continue her scheduled dermatology surveillance.

Occupational Health Service

Dermatology follow-up, date of service 01/23/2026. Received 01/27/2026.

18 months after wide local excision for stage IA melanoma of the back. Asymptomatic.

Allergies: penicillin (rash), dust mites.

Full skin and nodal examination: excision scar well healed with no recurrence. No new lesions of concern. No lymphadenopathy.

Impression: no evidence of disease. Continue every 6 month examinations and self-checks.

Dermatology follow-up, date of service 07/24/2026. Received 07/28/2026.

Two years from treatment of a stage IA melanoma of the back (pT1a). No new concerns.

Allergies: penicillin (rash), dust mites.

documents.body: Hi - time to book my yearly physical. Late September works best, any morning. I'd also like to go over colon cancer screening, since I turn 45 next June and want to have a plan.
